criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission, need with bleaching statistics, single-sat rationale, operator/customers all addressed with literature refs. Detail good though funding vague.

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All subtopics covered with STK views, access table, SSO plot. Weaknesses: RAAN justification wrong, equatorial benefit misapplied to SSO, no delta-V/link calc, Vega-E speculative, no STK files shown.

altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924°

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Summarises launch, orbit, ground station and risk. Largely repeats design, limited synthesis of evidence or quantitative outcomes.

evidence.quote: A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans
Alternatives include the earlier Vega C launcher

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings, exec summary, labelled STK plots/tables. OCR table breaks, inconsistent refs, truncated [10], Wikipedia used despite ban, some informal language.

technical_issues.issue: Claims equatorial launch saves fuel for retrograde SSO; ignores large plane-change penalty from 5deg site to 97.8deg orbit.
RAAN 27.33 deg said to indicate launch facility; RAAN is time-dependent, not site latitude. Argument of Latitude mis-presented as static element.
600km altitude vs 250km reef swath trade stated qualitatively; no sensor FOV, resolution, revisit calculation.
Proposes uncontrolled passive drag-sail deorbit but provides no area, mass, decay time or 25-year compliance estimate.

overall: Single-sat GBR fluid-lensing mission well-motivated with plausible SSO and STK access analysis, but launch rationale and orbital mechanics contain errors and quantitative support is limited.

feedback.summary: You proposed a well-motivated single-satellite GBR fluid-lensing mission with plausible SSO and STK access analysis. Your introduction and structure are strong, but launch rationale and orbital mechanics contain errors and quantitative support is limited. Focus on correcting mechanics, adding calculations, and synthesising conclusions with proper referencing.
next_steps: Correct your SSO launch and RAAN reasoning in Mission Design and add sensor, delta-V, link and deorbit sizing calculations with STK files.
Strengthen your Conclusion to synthesise quantitative outcomes from your evidence rather than repeating the design.
Fix referencing and professional style in Bibliography and throughout by completing reference [10] and replacing non-approved sources.

criteria.C1: You did well in your Executive Summary and Introduction to define coral reef monitoring, justify need with bleaching statistics, explain why only one satellite is required, and identify CSIRO/BOM users with literature refs. To reach top of Accomplished, clarify vague funding detail.
criteria.C2: You covered launch from Guiana Space Centre, 600km 97.7924° SSO in Image 1, manoeuvres, and ground access well with STK views. To reach Accomplished, fix equatorial benefit for retrograde SSO, RAAN 27.33 deg and Argument of Latitude errors, and add FOV, delta-V, link and drag-sail decay estimates.
criteria.C3: You summarised launch, polar SSO illumination, ground station and Vega C alternative in your Conclusion. To reach Accomplished, move beyond repetition to detailed conclusions drawn from your evidence with specific quantitative outcomes and residual risks.
criteria.C4: You used clear headings, executive summary, and labelled STK plots/tables in Images 1 and 4. To reach Accomplished, ensure consistent formatting, formal language, matching in-text and list references, complete all entries, and use only approved sources.
